Design tokens are vendored as pure Python (tokens.py) and mapped onto Streamlit 1.58's native theme keys (mapping.py) — ~120 keys exist, so the navy sidebar, dataframe header, chart palettes, radii and fonts are all reachable through the PUBLIC config API rather than CSS. config_writer.py renders that one mapping two ways — CLI flags (primary — a config.toml resolves relative to CWD, so only flags theme every launch identically) and a generated .streamlit/config.toml (fallback for a bare `streamlit run`). The committed config was hand-written with every value drifted (primaryColor `#08BCC2` vs the real `#14b4b4`, grey sidebar vs navy, "sans serif" vs Inter, no dark mode); 1.230 makes that unrepeatable by asserting the file is byte-identical to the generator. Fonts point at the frontend's OWN Google Fonts stylesheet via Streamlit's "<family>:<url>" form, so the two surfaces agree both connected (both Inter) and air-gapped (both fall back) — bundling a woff2 for Streamlit alone was rejected because the frontend does not bundle one either. 4 keys (chart ramps + showSidebarBorder) are global-only with no per-mode twin, pinned by 1.217b since Streamlit rejects unrecognised options outright. A broken theme never blocks a launch (1.229). Verified against real Streamlit — flags and generated TOML both accepted, launch survives a deliberately broken token module. Also fixes `lex streamlit` silently overriding a caller-supplied port — the hardcoded ports were appended AFTER the caller's args, so a custom port was ignored and the command was unusable wherever 8080 was already taken. The proxy's UPSTREAM now follows `--server.port`, so it cannot forward to a dead port (1.232-1.235). CLI flag values are emitted BARE — reusing the TOML encoder quoted them, so every colour arrived as `"#14b4b4"` and Streamlit silently skipped it as invalid; the theme applied nowhere while every shape-level check passed. 1.236 now asserts the values Streamlit actually RESOLVES. Streamlit's CLI cannot express list options at all, lists ARE expressible on the CLI (Streamlit json.loads them) so they stay JSON while scalars go bare, and the sequential/diverging ramps need EXACTLY 10 stops or Streamlit discards them for its own defaults — another silent skip (1.236c/1.236d). |
